## A building-services diagram you can read by clicking

Every **label in this drawing is a door**: a click publishes `en:…` on the diagram's `zones` channel, and both cards to
the right follow — the **article**, and its **traffic**.

- The zones are the drawing's **own words**, read out of the picture by OCR (14 runs, every one at confidence 1.00) —
  not hand-drawn boxes.
- One label needed judgement, not a lookup: the drawing spells it **"Condensor"**. The zone sits on that word and opens
  **Surface condenser**.
- Two parts of the drawing have no label at all — the chimney (`Flue gas`) and the steam circuit itself (`Rankine cycle`).
  They are deliberately *not* zones: a zone goes on something the drawing names.
- Note the opposite of a **tour** board: here the zones `send`, because the consumers want an *article*; on a tour the
  content zones must `open`, or the next view receives an article name where it wants a file.

*Image: MIT OpenCourseWare — 4.401 Introduction to Building Technology (Spring 2006). [Steam Turbine](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:MIT_4.401_Introduction_to_Building_Technology,_Spring_2006_-_Steam_Turbine_-_3040752949.jpg) · CC BY-SA 4.0.*
